experiments.question: Why does a transparent workload model (pitch-count leash / pitches-per-BF x opponent) miss batters faced so badly?
experiments.hypothesis: Errors concentrate in identifiable roles: openers/bulk relievers, season debuts, spot starters and short rest.
experiments.method: Segment validation errors of model D (opener flag, days since last appearance, debut, layoff, no start history, early exit); add those terms to a dev-fitted Poisson GLM (D_rc).
experiments.result: D validation MAE 2.813 -> D_rc 2.605 (CRPS 2.0345 -> 1.8851). Rest <=2 days elasticity -0.71, rest 3 -0.49, rest 4 -0.34 (log scale). Early exits (<=12 BF) are 4.3% of starts but 16.5% of D's absolute error.
experiments.interpretation: Days since the pitcher's last appearance is the single strongest workload signal: a 'starter' who pitched 1-4 days ago is an opener. Early exits (injury, blow-up) remain unforecastable from box scores.

experiments.question: Is the gradient-boosted model (E) better than the corrected transparent model for batters faced and outs?
experiments.hypothesis: Remaining nonlinear workload interactions (rest x recent pitch counts x role) are learnable.
experiments.method: Walk-forward LightGBM refitted every two months from 2023-04 on PIT features; frozen-winner rule on validation CRPS with a significance tie-break toward the transparent model.
experiments.result: BF: lowest validation CRPS: E; beats best transparent D_rc by -0.0583 CRPS [-0.0732, -0.0416]. Outs: lowest validation CRPS: F; beats best transparent C by -0.0274 CRPS [-0.035, -0.0195].
experiments.interpretation: The GBM's gain is broad: ordinary starters MAE D_rc 2.54 vs E 2.48; openers MAE D_rc 3.59 vs E 3.16; debuts MAE D_rc 3.22 vs E 2.97. It is frozen for the opportunity families with D_rc kept as the explainable fallback.

experiments.question: Does an opponent strikeout adjustment (team K% vs the pitcher's hand, shrunk) and park help strikeout projections?
experiments.hypothesis: Opponent K tendency scales a pitcher's K rate multiplicatively (elasticity ~1, log5).
experiments.method: C = BF(D_rc) x EB-shrunk K/BF; D = C x exp(b1 log opp_factor + b2 log park_factor), b fitted by Poisson likelihood on 2023-24.
experiments.data: Opponent K% vs LHP/RHP from the 2024-26 PA feed, overall team K% for earlier seasons; park K factor from prior games at the venue.
experiments.result: Fitted elasticities: opponent 1.01, park 0.45. Validation CRPS C 1.2570 -> D 1.2386; MAE 1.797 -> 1.765.
experiments.interpretation: The opponent elasticity is almost exactly the theoretical 1.0, and the adjustment is a clear, significant gain (not a fitted artefact).

experiments.question: Which distribution best represents strikeouts given a mean?
experiments.hypothesis: K | BF ~ Binomial(BF, p) mixed over the BF distribution captures both workload and rate uncertainty.
experiments.method: Development CRPS of Poisson, NB, binned NB, empirical residual and binomial-on-BF mixture (beta-binomial phi grid) for model D.
experiments.interpretation: The BF mixture is best, but every family is within ~0.1% CRPS: the mean is what matters; the shape is not the bottleneck.

experiments.question: Do pitch-level quality signals (prior whiff%, fastball velocity change) improve strikeout projections beyond K%?
experiments.hypothesis: Whiff rate beyond what K% shows, and velocity drops, predict strikeouts.
experiments.method: Poisson offset GLM on top of frozen D: fit 2026-08-25..09-08, test 09-09..09-27 (only window with Statcast in the repo).
experiments.data: 379 fit / 468 test starts with >=2 prior Statcast starts.
experiments.interpretation: No detectable gain; the window is 7 weeks, so this is 'no evidence of value at this depth', not proof of no value.

experiments.question: Is the frozen pitcher_strikeouts model better than the production pitcher engine (incumbent)?
experiments.hypothesis: Role-aware workload and opponent-adjusted rates beat the incumbent's single recency-weighted outs mean.
experiments.method: Matched 2026 holdout starts; incumbent = lib/research/pitcher_prop_projection.py re-run walk-forward (retroactive, as-of first pitch-60m). Rung RPS over the incumbent's own rungs, MAE, Brier at Kalshi rungs; game-clustered bootstrap.
experiments.interpretation: Better than the incumbent on every metric with intervals excluding zero; the incumbent rerun is retroactive, so this is a walk-forward comparison, not an archived-forecast one.

experiments.question: How much does knowing the batting slot (confirmed lineup) improve hitter projections?
experiments.hypothesis: PA depends strongly on slot; using only the previous slot loses accuracy when lineups change.
experiments.method: Same model D with the post-game official slot vs the player's previous slot (no lineup information).
experiments.result: PA (validation): CRPS prev-slot minus known-slot +0.0099 [+0.0089, +0.0110], slot changed in 41% of games; H (validation): CRPS prev-slot minus known-slot +0.0006 [+0.0004, +0.0008], slot changed in 41% of games; TB (validation): CRPS prev-slot minus known-slot +0.0008 [+0.0004, +0.0011], slot changed in 41% of games; R (validation): CRPS prev-slot minus known-slot +0.0005 [+0.0003, +0.0006], slot changed in 41% of games; RBI (validation): CRPS prev-slot minus known-slot +0.0001 [-0.0001, +0.0002], slot changed in 41% of games; HRR (validation): CRPS prev-slot minus known-slot +0.0013 [+0.0007, +0.0019], slot changed in 41% of games
experiments.interpretation: Lineup confirmation is worth a measurable amount for PA (and less for rate stats). Forecasts made before lineups post must use the prev-slot variant and be labelled.

experiments.question: Do opposing-starter quality, park and platoon adjust hitter rates usefully?
experiments.hypothesis: Hit rates scale with the starter's hits-allowed rate over his share of PAs, park and handedness.
experiments.method: D = C x exp(sum b_i x share x log factor_i); b fitted on 2024 (from May).
experiments.data: Starter PIT rates from the pitcher frame; park factors from prior games at the venue; league platoon multipliers fitted on 2024 PAs.
experiments.result: Hits elasticities sp_h +0.07, park_h +0.74, plat -0.14, sp_k -0.59, icpt -0.01. Validation CRPS C 0.4565 -> D 0.4552.
experiments.interpretation: Context adds a small, real improvement; most hitter variance is irreducible at the game level.

experiments.question: Which hitter distributions are best: Poisson/NB on the mean, empirical, binomial-on-PA, or TB convolution?
experiments.hypothesis: Hits ~ Binomial(PA, p) mixed over PA; total bases = convolution of per-PA base outcomes.
experiments.method: Development CRPS by candidate for model D.
experiments.result: Hits: poisson 0.4525; nb 0.4525; empirical_resid 0.4516; binom_mix(phi=0.01) 0.4512. TB: poisson 0.9147; nb 0.8772; empirical_resid 0.8762; tb_mix 0.8751
experiments.interpretation: Structural (binomial / convolution) shapes are at least as good as fitted ones and are coherent by construction.

experiments.question: Are the frozen hitter models better than the production hitter engine?
experiments.hypothesis: Per-PA EB rates with structural PA beat the incumbent's simulation (known +0.135 hits / -0.151 RBI bias, HITTER_W2_RESULTS).
experiments.method: Matched 2026 player-games where the incumbent re-run (archived pregame inputs) is PROJECTED; full CRPS from both pmfs.
experiments.interpretation: Consistent with the W2 audit: the incumbent's level biases dominate its error.

experiments.question: What does each layer of team-run context add (offence x opponent run prevention, starter, park, schedule adjustment)?
experiments.hypothesis: Following RSCH-0015, opponent strength helps the mean but may not help probability scores.
experiments.method: B EWMA vs C offence x defence (log5 on runs) vs D (+ starter share x starter runs factor + park + home) vs D_ridge (pf_core rolling ridge, weekly refits).
experiments.interpretation: Offence x opponent run prevention (C) improves both CRPS and MAE over the team's own EWMA on both splits; starter + park (D) improves CRPS on both splits and MAE only on holdout. Unlike RSCH-0015 (frozen NB), the probability gain survives because the distribution is fitted per model on development. Ridge schedule adjustment does not beat the raw shrunk factors (validation +0.0037 [+0.0005, +0.0073]).

experiments.question: Should the game total be the convolution of team distributions or a direct NB on the summed mean?
experiments.method: Holdout CRPS of the convolution vs a direct NB with alpha fitted on development totals.
experiments.result: Validation diff +0.0001 [-0.0011, +0.0011]; holdout diff +0.0005 [-0.0006, +0.0015]; direct NB alpha 0.1295.
experiments.interpretation: The two are near-identical; the convolution is kept because it is coherent with the team projections.

experiments.question: Is the team-run model better than the archived production projection?
experiments.hypothesis: RSCH-0033 found the production mean biased (-0.33 runs) with slope ~1.
experiments.method: Only archived projections whose file createdAt precedes first pitch (genuinely pregame); incumbent distribution = NB with RSCH-0010's 0.2815 dispersion.
experiments.interpretation: The model removes the incumbent's level bias (-0.34 runs, matching RSCH-0033's -0.33) but the CRPS difference is not significant on this short archived-pregame window (parity).

experiments.question: Do hitter run projections reconcile with team run projections?
experiments.hypothesis: Sum of starters' projected runs ~= team runs x starters' share of runs.
experiments.method: pf_core.gate.team_reconciliation per team-game on the 2026 holdout.
experiments.result: Starters score 94.4% of runs; mean sum of starters' R 4.2465 vs team 4.5068; ratio 0.9985; correlation 0.9302; reconciliation {'PASS': 4854}.
experiments.interpretation: Hitter and team models are built independently yet agree in level; per-game spread differs because team context (opponent run prevention) is richer than the hitter R model.

opponent_adjustment.summary: Opponent adjustments are multiplicative factors (shrunk, point-in-time) whose elasticities are fitted on development. Pitcher K: opponent elasticity 1.01, park 0.45; hits allowed opponent 1.16; walks 1.27. Team runs: offence x opponent run prevention (log5) then starter share x starter run factor and park.

failed_experiments.name: Pitch-level Statcast (whiff%, velocity change) for strikeouts

failed_experiments.name: Structural pitch-count leash model for batters faced (C/D)
failed_experiments.what_was_learned: Pitches EWMA / pitches-per-BF ignores role; it over-projects openers by ~3.5 BF.
failed_experiments.changes_future_decisions: Workload models must condition on days since last appearance and recent relief usage.

failed_experiments.name: Schedule-adjusted ridge team ratings (D_ridge)
failed_experiments.what_was_learned: No improvement over raw shrunk offence/defence factors: +0.0037 [+0.0005, +0.0073] CRPS on validation.
failed_experiments.changes_future_decisions: Keep the simpler PIT factors; MLB schedules are balanced enough that schedule adjustment matters little.
